thread:
rebecca-sales: Quick help — Orbis demo Monday. They want 99p <= 350ms and are willing to commit to an enterprise tier. Traffic: baseline ~5 rps, peak bursts ~40 rps for ~10m, daily tokens ~1.2M (75% short <=64t, 25% long >=512t). What reserved GPU sizing + autoscale policy should I propose? Also they asked about prewarm/KV strategies and pricing uplift for reserved capacity.

mike-eng: thanks — couple quick Qs: is their traffic spiky across regions or single region? and do long requests mostly happen in bursts or spread out?

rebecca-sales: single region (us-east-1). long requests are bursty (tied to nightly batch ops) but some ad-hoc long completions during daytime spikes.

ashley-se: my take: start with 2 x A100-80GB reserved for baseline and steady load, add 1 reserved prewarmed slot for long/large batches, then autoscale up to +2 burst GPUs (on demand) for the 40 rps spikes. That gives headroom and keeps 99p latency under 350ms for short chats if we tune batching. Recommend KV prefix prewarm for top 200 prompts.

mike-eng: sounds reasonable. ballpark throughput: with current model (redwood-llama-13b-int8) ~ short requests → ~1200 tok/s per GPU w/ batching, long requests drop due to decoding cost. So 2 reserved GPUs cover baseline + steady long jobs; bursts require the +2.

ashley-se: sample autoscale policy I'd pitch:
```json
{
  "min_reserved": 2,
  "prewarm_slots": 1,
  "scale_up_policy": "if cpu_util>65% OR queue_depth>20 -> add 1 gpu (cooldown 60s)",
  "max_burst": 2,
  "latency_target_ms": 300
}
```
Explain to Orbis that prewarm_slot is for KV and model weights pinned to avoid coldstart.

ben-infra: add notes on spot/eviction fallback: ensure reserved pool is zonal-spread (2 AZs) and burst GPUs can be spot with an automatic fallback route to a smaller quantized model (zhippo-quant-v2) if eviction occurs. Also set autoscale cooldowns to 60–90s to avoid flapping.

sam-pm: pricing ask — for this commit (monthly token + 3-reserved GPU baseline with burst credits), we can offer ~15% discount vs on-demand. Need final numbers on expected token/day and expected burst hours to calc ARR. Rebecca can you confirm contract length?

rebecca-sales: they are looking at 12–18 months. I'll estimate burst hours: expecting ~3h/day at peak historically, so ~90h/month.

mike-eng: quick calc: reserved 3 GPUs (2 base + 1 prewarm) + average 1 burst GPU for 3h/day gives effective hours: reserved 24/7 for 3 GPUs = 2160 GPU-hours/month, burst 1 * 90 = 90h -> 2250h total. With autoscale max 2 burst, billing still counts hours used. We'll provide exact per-GPU-per-hour rate in the quote.

rebecca-sales: perfect — I'll draft the presales handoff doc with these numbers and the autoscale snippet. tagging @ashley-se for a short presales runbook and @ben-infra for AZ/spot fallback bullets. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment note: prewarm job scheduled — create prewarm image and KV load job 24h before demo if commit signed.

ashley-se: I'll add the KV prompt list and a small runbook: steps to load top 200 prefixes, run a 10m smoke at 40 rps, check 99p. Also recommend we include a canary model (quantized) and an automatic fallback route in the config.

rebecca-sales: thanks, team. I'll circulate handoff doc + price sketch to Orbis and ask for confirmation before Friday.

mike-eng: good plan — happy to join the call if they want a technical handover.

rebecca-sales: will do. end of thread.
